What I changed in Change Stack

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

I kept the layer-based review model and focused on staying oriented while checking an explanation against code. The original already has summary navigation and explicit viewed status. I changed their presentation and added a return path for one cross-file inspection.

What got in the wayWhat I changed
File identity and controls compete with the code.The file list stays available in the rail. A fixed layer switcher keeps all seven layers reachable when files are expanded. Outline sits beside the code; occasional file actions stay in Tools.
A broad summary range leaves the supporting statement to find.Short behavior labels link to code; the full source wording is one click away. Inspect guard opens feedback-access.ts. Return to access.ts restores the caller. The anchors are manually mapped starting points.
File context and layer context need different scopes.This file shows the selected explanation. Entire layer starts with compact summary rows across the nine paths. Scope and tabs stay fixed while context scrolls. Coverage is explicit: 14 of 37 summaries captured.
File viewed, summary seen and PR status mean different things.The header tracks seven included diffs; the rail tracks nine layer files. Viewed remains deliberate, with Undo. The merged snapshot disables Submit review; a separate open-PR demo shows that flow.

Keep the code readable

Wrapped 13 px code trades horizontal movement for vertical scrolling. Added-file Split uses a 96 px Before rail; Equal panes restores 50/50. A direct anchor is a starting point: surrounding code and the complete source summary stay available.

Checks and limits

I checked direct code links, guard/return navigation, context scopes, progress and Undo, notes, Copy path, the six entities and keyboard access. The 1440 px, 1280 px and 1100 px layouts passed. These are implementation checks; developer testing remains outstanding.

What I’d test next

My hypothesis is less searching and backtracking without losing comprehension. I’d ask developers to explain the access check, inspect its guard, then return. Compare wrong turns and explanation accuracy against the original. Modified-file review and stale anchors need testing.
